references.title: Home: an enclosed, personal place
references.story: revision/latest.md:61–81; central room, branching halls and adjacent private rooms. script.rpy:51–52; garden folds around the home.
references.observed: A central table, books and drawings, close seating, a small fountain and several arched thresholds. The room feels occupied and sheltered.
references.proposal: Treat this as the shared central room of one connected dwelling. Account for the whole household program: private rooms and adult retreats, Arin’s workshop, Selene’s music room, Dorian’s library, Sage’s room, cooking, art and practical support. Some attachments and overlaps remain unresolved. Its garden is ordinary household outdoor space.
references.unknown: The frame does not show the whole dwelling or establish its area. Separate arches are not separate houses. The author identifies the household garden as ordinary, without an implication of unusual wealth.

pins.text: Table, books and work in progress establish everyday occupation.
Successive arches connect parts of a dwelling; private rooms continue beyond this shared room.
Household outdoor space can adjoin the room without making every planted space public.

references.title: Arin’s workshop: making, learning and ongoing projects
references.observed: Broad rear workbench and side benches/drawers, tools and small mechanisms, stool, timber floor, planted window left and doorway right.
references.proposal: Closely associated with home life; the VN opening hears its hum and the daily montage returns here. Its doorway opens to further planted interior space in the art.
references.unknown: Exact attachment to the dwelling and work/service access. Do not replace it with Soren’s workshop, the construction equipment room or a generic community workroom. Preserve both personal experimentation and useful engineering.

pins.text: An equipped bench carries mechanisms and work in progress.
Drawers, tools and open floor support the hands-on workshop scenes.
An arched doorway continues into planted interior space; its destination is not established.

references.title: Selene’s music room: practice and shared learning
references.observed: Piano and shared bench center, harp and soft seating right, hallway doorway left and planted window openings.
references.proposal: Within the home’s soundscape; the VN explicitly approaches Selene’s door along a hall.
references.unknown: Acoustic/privacy control and room dimensions; possible relationship to Selene’s personal retreat. Sound must still reach the home in the existing scenes.

pins.text: The piano and shared bench support Cali and Selene’s lesson.
The harp and nearby cushions need their own usable space.
The doorway connects to a hall, also explicit in the scene text.

references.title: Dorian’s library: maps, reading and stories

references.proposal: A recurring destination in the family routine. Its exact connection to the home’s central room is not mapped.
references.unknown: Exact attachment, archive extent and use by outside listeners. Do not reduce it to the central room’s bookshelf or identify it as the whole community archive.

pins.text: A map table and surrounding cushions form a reading and storytelling area.
Books and scrolls occupy the room, with additional work surfaces below.
The rear arch opens to a corridor; its route to the home remains to be placed.

references.proposal: In the home; the fountain can be heard beyond Sage’s door.
references.unknown: Precise adjacency and degree of acoustic/visual privacy. This household room does not establish that professional transition counseling always happens here.

pins.text: A furnished sleeping alcove is part of the room’s visual guide.
The low table and cushions provide room for Sage and the three children.
The text hears the household fountain beyond this door; exact adjacency is open.

references.title: Soren’s workshop: a distinct place for systems work
references.observed: Drafting bench and plans, tool drawers, work surfaces, floor rover prototype and arched corridor at right; distinct from Arin’s shop.
references.proposal: Associated with Joren’s family home; exact attachment is unspecified.
references.unknown: Work/service access, noise and equipment needs. Keep this separate from Arin’s personal workshop and the construction equipment room.

pins.text: The drafting bench and plans support the rover design scene.

The arched passage provides visible depth without establishing attachment to Joren’s home.

pins.text: Tea and drawings occupy the central table and nearby seating.

references.title: Courtyard: social life among cultivated structure
references.story: revision/latest.md:57; connected paths, gardens and plazas
references.observed: A low shared table is surrounded by intimate seating, planted edges and curved adjoining passages. Light is filtered through canopy.
references.proposal: Distinguish courts used by nearby households from household interiors and gardens, and from larger community plazas. Connect them through shared paths and recognizable domestic thresholds.
references.unknown: This frame does not establish that every court has the same plan, or that all residents share this one court.

pins.text: Seated people and the table establish a small social scale.
A curved passage carries the scene beyond its immediate gathering space.
Canopy and planted overhead connections create filtered enclosure.

references.title: Garden and oak: two related inhabited heights
references.runtime: bg garden · visuals.rpy:12 · script.rpy:177; treehouse entrance sequence
references.story: revision/latest.md: treehouse chapters; oak, ladder and separate lower hollow
references.observed: The upper room sits among the oak branches. A ladder meets its right-hand entrance; a separate lower hollow and broad seating refuge occupy the bank below.
references.proposal: Give the oak genuine rooting depth and canopy clearance in the broader shared wooded garden edge. Keep the nearby household garden distinct from the more shared treehouse surroundings; preserve the upper entrance, ladder and lower refuge.
references.unknown: This oak is not the Tree of Echoes. Its visible scale does not determine the material or size of Lumen’s main structural supports.

pins.text: Upper room: handmade, inhabited and sheltered by branches.
The ladder connects to the upper entrance; the lower hollow is separate.
A broad refuge sits at garden level. Root and drainage volume must fit beneath it.

references.unknown: The CG does not calibrate exact water depth. It does not justify converting the pond to a deep reservoir, canal or exposed drop.

pins.text: Hands and low bank make the rescue physically readable.
A small basin supports the scene; exact depth requires comparison with the background.
Dry standing/kneeling room and familiar access are part of the place.

references.unknown: The painted supports’ wood-like appearance does not identify the load-bearing material throughout the vessel.

references.unknown: The projected design is not a ship plan, a canon gravity mechanism or proof that every wall can instantly transform.

references.proposal: Use branching inhabited structure and multiple connected view volumes. The local overlook reveals a wider pattern without displaying the whole ship.
references.unknown: No exterior silhouette, exact span, total population, roof type or single global ground plane can be measured from this image.

pins.text: Foreground platform and scaffold establish the local ascent viewpoint.
Many occupied heights overlap through depth; this is the central spatial relationship to preserve.
Rooms, foliage and supports continue beyond the immediate opening.

references.unknown: Visible galleries do not establish total gathering capacity. Keep the manuscript’s whole-community claim open for a measured test; do not infer a census from painted heads.

references.title: Tree of Echoes: a distinct heritage grove
references.story: revision/latest.md: Tree of Echoes passage; wiki/worldbuilding/Lumen.md

references.proposal: Place this as a quieter, distinct place within the garden network. Give its tree a credible root zone; preserve its role in Lumen’s gradual revelation.
references.unknown: The tree is not evidence for a sole ship-wide trunk, a central brain or the oak treehouse’s location.

pins.text: The hollow heritage tree remains distinct from the children’s oak.
Layered canopy and enclosure make a sheltered, reflective place.
Small local light sources shape mood; they do not establish the crop-energy supply.
